source: That branch of the lake of Como which extends southwards between two unbroken chains of mountains, and is all bays and gulfs as the mountains advance and recede, narrows down at one point into the form of a river, between a promontory on one side and a wide shore on the other; and the bridge which here links the two banks seems to emphasize this transformation, and to mark the point at which the lake ends and the Adda begins, only to become a lake once more where the banks draw farther apart again, letting the water broaden out and expand into new gulfs and bays. The country bordering the lake, formed by the deposits of three great torrents, is backed by two neighbouring mountains, one called San Martino, and the other, in the Lombard dialect, the Resegone, from its saw-like row of peaks; so that on first seeing it — so long as it is in profile — looking northwards, for instance, from the ramparts of Milan — one can pick it out at once, on the name alone, from the vast and lengthy range of other mountains of obscurer name and more ordinary form. For a considerable stretch the country rises slowly and continuously; then it breaks up into little hills and valleys and into steep and level tracts, following the structure of the two mountains and the erosion of the water. The shore itself, intersected by the beds of torrents, is almost entirely gravel and pebbles; the rest is fields and vineyards, and scattered towns, villages and farms, with here and there a wood extending right on up the mountain-side. Lecco, which is the largest of these towns and gives its name to the district, lies on the lakeside not far from the bridge, and is even apt to find itself partly in the lake when this is high; it is a big town nowadays, well on the way to becoming a city. At the time of the events which we are about to describe, this township which was already of some importance, was also fortified, and so had the honour of housing a commandant and the advantage of a permanent garrison of Spanish soldiers, who taught modesty to the wives and daughters of the town, tickled up the shoulders of an occasional husband and father, and, towards the end of summer, never failed to scatter themselves among the vineyards, to thin out the grapes and lighten the labours of the vintage for the peasants. Paths and tracks used to run — and still do — from one to another of these villages, from the mountain heights to the lakeside, and from one precipice to the other. Sometimes they run steep, sometimes level, and often drop suddenly and bury themselves between two walls, from which, when one looks up, only a patch of sky and some mountain peak can be discerned. Sometimes they come out on open terraces; thence the eye ranges over prospects of varying extent, always full of interest and always changing, as each point of vantage takes in different aspects of the vast landscape, and as one part or the other is foreshortened, or stands out, or disappears. One can see a piece here, another there, and then again a long stretch of that great varied mirror of the water; on this side the lake is shut in at one end, or rather lost among the ins and outs and groupings of the mountains, then spreads out again between more mountains, unfolding one by one, and reflected upside down in the water with the villages on the shores; on the other side is more river, then lake, then river again, losing itself in a shining coil among the mountains, which follow it, getting smaller and smaller until they too are almost lost in the horizon. The very spot from which so many different views can be seen itself appears in views from every side. The mountain on whose foothills you are walking unfolds its cliffs and pinnacles above and around you, each standing out on its own and changing at every step, turning what had just seemed a single ridge into a whole series of ridges, and showing on a height something that a moment before had seemed down on the shore; the quiet and cosy character of these foothills pleasantly tempers the wildness around, and is a foil for the grandeur of the rest of the landscape.

rows.text:
The waters that the night patrols divide, and the thermal cameras that they calibrate to teach, and the outreach workers who shelter and who counsel, and the registration forms that guide and that protect, and the holding facilities that receive and that prepare, and the liaison officers who accompany and who reassure—all this benevolent architecture of care, as the vessels that it intercepts and the channels that it monitors and the coordinates that it shares and the alerts that it transmits and the networks that it maintains and the protocols that it observes and the databases that it populates and the risk assessments that it refines and the partnerships that it cultivates and the capacities that it builds would testify, should one ask them, to shelter those who cross, to guide those who wander, to receive those who arrive, this apparatus unfolds where the sea meets the rock, and where the rock meets the wire, and where the wire meets the beam, and where the beam meets the shadow, and where the shadow meets the craft, and where the craft meets the hand, and where the hand meets the document, and where the document meets the stamp, and where the stamp meets the file, and where the file meets the archive, and where the archive meets the forgetting, and where the forgetting meets the return, and where the return meets the water again, and where the water again meets the patrol, and where the patrol again meets the night, and where the night again meets the counting, and where the counting again meets the report, and where the report again meets the policy, and where the policy again meets the sea.

The island that the currents shape, which the fishermen once knew by their nets' drag and their catch's weight, which the pilots now read through instruments that speak in frequencies the ear cannot hear, and which the algorithms parse into vectors of probability and zones of intervention, stands where the African plate presses beneath the European, and where the depths that swallow light have swallowed also the hulls of those who calculated badly, or who were betrayed by engines, or who were abandoned by captains, or who simply ran out of fuel before they ran out of hope, to drift, to founder, to become the data points that populate the dashboards of the agencies that monitor, that respond, that coordinate, that prevent.

The wind rises, and the surge answers, and the vessels hold or do not hold their stations.

The cliffs that the winter storms erode, which the gulls colonize with their noise and their guano, which the engineers measure for their rate of retreat and their load-bearing capacity, and which the planners mark as heritage or as hazard according to the funding cycle's phase, present a face of limestone and a face of tufa, of porous stone and compacted ash, of the ancient sea's own architecture and the more ancient volcano's, of what holds water and what releases it, of what resists the pick and what yields to the hammer, of what the builder prizes and what the builder curses, of what the rain dissolves slowly and what the frost shatters suddenly.

The horizon that the dawn redefines, and the horizon that the dusk withdraws, and the horizon that the fog erases, and the horizon that the clear air restores, and the horizon that the instruments project beyond the visible, and the horizon that the regulations establish as jurisdictional limit, and the horizon that the rescue craft must reach before it becomes a search for survivors rather than a recovery of remains, and the horizon that the families in distant cities scan on their screens, waiting for coordinates, waiting for names, waiting for the silence to become information, this horizon moves, and is moved, and is measured, and is managed, and is mourned.

The port that the ferries serve, and the port that the naval vessels use, and the port that the fishing boats abandon when the stocks decline, and the port that the tourists photograph, and the port that the journalists write from, and the port that the migrants remember, and the port that the migrants forget, and the port that the statistics aggregate, and the port that the policies target, and the port that the histories omit, and the port that the novels discover, and the port that the poems resist, this port collects and disperses, receives and expels, anchors and releases, marks and erases, names and renames, according to the document that governs, the stamp that authorizes, the signature that certifies, the date that locates, the file that preserves, the term that expires, the renewal that continues, the practice that hardens into custom, the custom that hardens into law, the law that requires the practice to change.

The light that the lighthouse casts, which the mariners read for their position, which the smugglers read for their opportunity, which the patrols read for their interception, and which the cameras capture for their archives, falls on water that swells and that contracts, that opens and that closes, that receives and that rejects, that promises and that withdraws, that the same word names as passage and as barrier, as route and as obstacle, as the element that connects and the element that divides, as the medium of movement and the agent of stillness, as what the body must cross and what the body cannot cross, as what the law governs and what the law cannot reach, as what the document records and what the document cannot record, as what the instrument measures and what the instrument cannot measure, as what the eye sees and what the eye cannot see, as what the memory holds and what the memory cannot hold.

The radar turns, and the screen pulses, and the operator watches.

The night that the infrared penetrates, and the night that the darkness preserves, and the night that the silence amplifies, and the night that the engine sound betrays, and the night that the satellite witnesses, and the night that the database remembers, and the night that the morning will dissolve into statistics, and the night that the morning will not dissolve for those who do not reach it, this night accumulates, layer upon layer, signal upon signal, absence upon absence, until the threshold is crossed, the protocol activated, the response mounted, the rescue attempted, the recovery completed, the forms filled, the notifications sent, the case closed, the file archived, the space cleared for the next night, which will resemble this one, which resembles the one before, which resembles the pattern that the analysts identify, that the policymakers address, that the public forgets, that the sea receives.

The bodies that the currents deliver, and the bodies that the currents keep, and the bodies that the currents distribute according to laws the living do not know, and the bodies that the living must identify, must number, must photograph, must store, must match to names, must match to reports, must match to families, must return or must bury, must memorialize or must forget, these bodies mark the sea's own accounting, its own record-keeping, its own archive of movement and arrest, of departure and non-arrival, of intention and interruption, of the desire that launched the vessel and the force that ended it, of the hope that sustained the voyage and the calculation that failed it, of the hand that paid the fare and the hand that steered toward disaster, of the voice that said go and the voice that said wait and the silence that followed both.

The island remains, and the patrols continue, and the water moves as it has moved, as we write, as we read, as the next vessel prepares, as the next alert registers, as the next decision waits upon the next assessment, upon the next forecast, upon the next policy, upon the next funding round, upon the next election, upon the next crisis that will make visible what the present crisis obscures, that will name what the present naming cannot name, that will count what the present counting cannot count, that will reach what the present reaching cannot reach, before the water closes over, before the file closes upon, before the eye turns elsewhere, before the memory releases what it has held too long, or not long enough.

The instructors who guide the frightened toward waiting vessels, who shepherd the exhausted into processing tents, who teach the protocols of documentation to those who have fled across the waters—these pedagogues of passage work their curriculum of care upon the salt-crusted bodies that the night fishermen, whose lamps still drift upon the horizon where the dark swells meet the darker sky, have hauled from the inflatable rafts that the thermal cameras, which the engineers who designed them intended for search and rescue, now track as vectors of risk to be intercepted before they reach the shore where the volunteers, who believe themselves merciful, distribute blankets and water bottles while the biometric scanners, which the technicians who calibrated them meant to expedite mercy, harvest the templates of irises that the databases, which the analysts who maintain them understand as protective instruments, will hold until the appeals expire and the removals can proceed according to the schedules that the administrators who draft them call managed mobility, and all this instruction in assistance unfolds beneath the surveillance drones whose gentle hum the operators, trained in humanitarian optics, have learned to distinguish from the sound of predation.

The waves that break upon the eastern rocks, where the lighthouse keeper, whose rotation ended three days past, left the logbook open to a page that records the weather as moderate and the traffic as routine, and the currents that drag their debris through the channel where the naval patrol, whose mandate shifts with each communique from the capital, now steers its intercept course, and the tides that expose the rusted hull of the vessel that sank in the year when the conventions were drafted to prevent such deaths, all move beneath a sky that the meteorologists, whose models now predict a calm that will last until the next system approaches from the northwest, have already named in their reports.

The swell rises and the swell falls, and the night comes and the night goes.

The fishermen who set their nets before dawn, and the pilots who guide their aircraft through the corridors that the controllers have designated for visual reconnaissance, watch the same water.

The refugees who learn to describe their journeys to the interpreters who are trained to detect inconsistencies, and who must learn to present their fear in forms that the case officers who evaluate them recognize as legitimate, and the officers themselves who must learn to apply the criteria that the courts who review their decisions have progressively narrowed, all participate in a pedagogy of documentation that the manuals who prescribe its steps intend to reduce to procedure, and the lawyers who challenge the procedures find themselves arguing before judges who have learned their own craft in the years when the conventions meant something different than they mean today.

The thermal signature that the operator observes upon his screen, which the algorithm that processes the feed has flagged as vessel-sized and moving at drift velocity, and the silhouette that resolves through his binoculars into the shape of an inflatable overloaded with bodies that the night has rendered indistinct, and the radio transmission that he must compose in the protocol that the headquarters who drafted it require for all contacts, and the coordinates that he must record in the log that the inspectors who review such logs will examine for compliance, all pass through the medium of his attention, which the training that prepared him for this station taught him to regard as a technical instrument rather than a moral faculty, and which now presents to his consciousness, simultaneously, the image of the sea as surface upon which objects move and the image of the sea as depth into which objects disappear, and these two images, which the optics that mediate them do not distinguish, overlay upon his retina in a superposition that he experiences not as contradiction but as duty.

The sea dilates.

The sea contracts.

The sea dilates again.

The vessel that the satellite has tracked since it departed the coast that the cartographers who revised the charts last spring still mark as disputed, and that the patrol craft which received the intercept order at 0347 has now approached to hailing distance, carries upon its deck a cargo that the law, in the document that the ratification instruments have deposited with the depository, designates as persons, and that the same law, in the subsequent protocol that the accession instruments have modified, designates as irregular movers, and the moment of this designation's application falls not upon any visible feature of the scene but upon the invisible boundary that the coordinates that the navigation system displays have crossed, and this crossing, which no passenger upon the vessel can perceive, triggers the jurisdiction that the agreements have allocated and the procedures that the manuals have prescribed.

The officer observes.

The officer records.

The officer transmits.

The officer waits.

The response that the headquarters returns, which the encryption that protects it renders accessible only to the terminal that the officer carries, and the instruction that this response contains, which the protocols that govern such communications require him to acknowledge before he acts, and the delay that this acknowledgment introduces, which the currents that move the vessel exploit to carry it further into the zone that the competing mandates have rendered ambiguous, and the decision that the officer must make, which the training that prepared him for this moment has not equipped him to make with confidence, all unfold in a present that the log that will record them will render as past, and this rendering, which the procedures require, will strip from the moment the hesitation that the officer now feels and replace it with the certainty that the genre of the report demands.

The waves that the wind has raised since the officer began his watch, and the clouds that have gathered since the forecast that the meteorologists issued at 1800, and the visibility that has degraded since the first light that the dawn promised, and the anxiety that has accumulated since the vessel first appeared upon his screen, all now press upon his attention in a convergence that the protocols do not address, and this convergence, which his training has taught him to regard as distraction, he now recognizes as the actual texture of the event that the manuals have abstracted into decision points, and this recognition, which occurs without words and without the sanction of any procedure, marks a fracture in the professional self that his preparation has constructed, and through this fracture there pours, not quite as thought and not quite as image, the memory of his own crossing, which his file records as family reunification and which his body records differently.

The migrants huddle.

The officers process.

The lawyers appeal.

The judges defer.

The sea receives what the sea receives.

The thermal camera that now tracks the second vessel that the algorithm has detected, which approaches from the bearing that the first vessel has drifted toward, and the inflatable that this camera resolves into the image of a craft whose motor has failed and whose passengers have begun, the posture of their bodies indicates, to understand their situation as terminal, and the patrol craft that the officer has requested and that the dispatch that the headquarters has transmitted has authorized, and the medical team that the protocol requires for all intercepts involving persons in distress, and the holding facility that the reception procedures designate as the destination for all persons intercepted in the operational zone, all now converge upon a coordinate that the navigation system renders as present position and that the law renders as jurisdictional threshold, and this rendering, which the instruments perform automatically, the officer must now perform consciously, choosing between the designation that the conventions have established and the designation that the subsequent instruments have modified, and this choice, which no manual addresses, he makes in the full knowledge that whatever he decides will be reviewed by bodies that were not present and will be recorded in forms that permit no ambiguity, and this knowledge, which his training has taught him to regard as accountability, he now experiences as the evacuation of judgment itself.

The night falls.

The migrants who the sea has claimed since the records that the statisticians compile began their count, and the vessels that the currents have distributed across the seafloor that the cartographers who survey it have begun to map as maritime cemetery, and the names that the survivors have carried to the offices where the caseworkers who receive them must reconcile them with the databases that the technicians maintain, and the stories that these names anchor, which the procedures that govern testimony require to be recorded in forms that the adjudicators who review them can evaluate for consistency, all now accumulate in an archive that the institutions who sustain it understand as documentation and that the institutions who resist it understand as accusation, and this accumulation, which proceeds without any single intention directing it, now constitutes a text that future readers, if such readers come, will read as the trace of a violence that the present has not learned to name as such.

The officer completes his report.

The vessel that the dawn has revealed upon the eastern beach, where the tide that has receded since the night has left it stranded among the debris that the currents deposit, and the bodies that the volunteers who have arrived since the first light have discovered within it, and the documents that the survivors among these bodies have preserved through the crossing that killed their companions, and the fingerprints that the technicians who have arrived since the volunteers have notified them will extract from these documents for comparison against the databases that the analysts search for matches, all now enter the procedures that the manuals prescribe for such discoveries, and these procedures, which the training that prepared the technicians for this work has rendered automatic, proceed in a rhythm that the scene itself does not dictate, and this rhythm, which the protocols establish as efficiency, produces a temporality in which the dead wait and the living wait and the distinction between these conditions, which the law maintains, becomes difficult to perceive beneath the glare that the morning has established and the heat that will intensify as the day progresses and the smells that the sun will release from the vessel and from the bodies that remain within it.

The patrol craft that circle Lampedusa, whose engines the fishermen learn to read before dawn, whose floodlights they call the second moon, and whose hulls scrape the limestone where no charts mark the depth, come to teach the crossing, to instruct the waiting, to guide the foundering toward what the manuals name rescue, and to lift from the water those whom the same manuals, in another column, record as intercepted, as diverted, as processed, as removed—these vessels that the islanders have learned to count like weather, and whose wake patterns the older men pretend not to study, move tonight across a swell that carries, beneath its measured heave, the cold current from the Sicilian channel and the warmer salt that rises from the African shelf, and the boats that will try tomorrow to thread between them, or next week, or in the season when the mistral empties the sky of even the guide stars, have already begun to gather at the Tunisian ports, or at the Libyan anchorages where the smugglers, who are also teachers, also instructors, also guides, weigh fuel against distance and the probability of encounter, which is to say of being taught, of being instructed, of being guided, so that the horizon, which the radar renders as a green circumference, and the horizon, which the eye retains as a trembling line, and the horizon, which the memory stores as the last visible land, become three horizons, and the craft that dissolve one into another, that translate floodlight into starlight into the phosphorescence the oars disturb, that convert the waiting into the crossing and the crossing into the waiting that follows, move now, as they have moved since the base was established and the agreements signed and the memoranda exchanged and the funding cycles renewed, across waters that the same documents name now as contiguous zone, now as search-and-rescue region, now as external border, now as the sea.

The fishermen, who remember when the lights meant only other fishermen, and who learned, before any manual instructed them, to read the particular pitch of diesel engines as a notation of distance and intention, and who have passed this knowledge to sons who will pass it to sons who will fish these waters when the current crisis, as the briefings term it, has been resolved or displaced or renamed, rise before the patrols and return after them, so that their own boats, which carry no floodlights and no radar and no manuals of instruction, cross the same waters under the same stars, though the stars, as the fishermen know and as the manuals do not record, shift their rising and setting across the year, and the pole star, which the smugglers also use, holds its place only for those who know to look for it, and the craft that will attempt the crossing tonight, or tomorrow night, or on the night when the sea that has been swelling begins to swell less and the wind that has been rising begins to rise less, have already been loaded with fuel that has been calculated against the probability of encounter, which the smugglers, who are not in the manuals, estimate differently than the patrols, who are, so that the same stretch of water, which the charts measure in nautical miles and the fishermen in hours of tacking and the patrols in response times and the crossed in hours of waiting and hours of fear and the hours that collapse these categories, will tonight, as it has for years, as it will for years, receive the vessels that the documents name irregular and the bodies they name irregular and the movement they name irregular, though the water itself, which receives all vessels and returns what it will not keep, recognizes no such category.

The swell rises and the swell falls, and in the hours before dawn the fishermen mend nets and the patrols calibrate equipment and the waiting continues, and the sea that was wide becomes wider and then less wide, and the horizon that was distant becomes more distant and then less distant, as the mistral empties the air and fills it and empties it again.

The craft that left Zuwarah three days prior, or that will leave tomorrow, or that left and were turned back and left again, carry those who have learned, in other waters, to read the signs of approach, and who will learn, in these waters, to read the signs of approach differently, or to misread them, or to read them correctly and find that correct reading alters nothing, and the patrols that approach them, whose floodlights announce intention before voice or gesture can, and whose manuals prescribe the sequence of announcement and approach and identification and assistance or interception, move across waters that the same manuals, in their different editions, have named differently, so that the assistance that was prescribed becomes, across a line invisible on the water, the interception that is prescribed, and the vessels that received one name receive another, and the names that were given are withdrawn and other names given, and the bodies that the names name remain, until they do not, in the water.

To turn and to return, to approach and to withdraw, to assist and to intercept, these are the motions that the manuals prescribe and that the patrols execute and that the fishermen observe, and the sea that receives all motion and returns it as current and as swell and as the particular sound that hulls make against limestone where no charts mark the depth, moves tonight as it moved last year and as it will move when the current agreements have expired and been renewed and expired again, and the craft that cross it, which the fishermen have learned to count and to name and to predict, move also, and the waiting that precedes them and the waiting that follows them moves also, so that the motion of the water and the motion of the vessels and the motion of those who wait to become vessels and the motion of those who wait to receive them become one motion, which the documents name crisis and the fishermen name weather and the patrols name operation and the crossed name the night or the day or the hour that remains.

The radar screen, which the watch officer consults and which consults nothing, shows the green circumference of detection, and beyond it the absence that is also presence, and the phosphorescence that the patrol boat's wake disturbs, which is the same phosphorescence that the fishing boats disturb and that the craft trying tonight to evade detection disturb, records in its brief luminosity the passage of all vessels, and the watch officer, who has learned to read this screen as the fishermen learned to read the stars and as the crossed learn to read the floodlights, marks a contact and marks its disappearance and marks its reappearance, and the manual that governs this marking prescribes the sequence of verification and approach and identification, and the manual that governs this sequence prescribes also the termination of sequence, which is to say the return to waiting, which is itself a sequence, and the sea that receives this waiting and returns it as hours and as days and as the years that the agreements cover and do not cover, moves tonight in its two motions, the motion of expansion and the motion of constriction, so that the vessels that were distant become near and the vessels that were near become distant, and the horizon that contained them releases them and receives them and releases them again.

The base at Lampedusa, which the documents name operational and the fishermen name the lights and the islanders name simply there, processes what it receives and returns what it cannot process, and the processing that it performs and the returning that it performs occur across a boundary that the same documents mark and do not mark, so that the processed and the returned bear different names though they have crossed the same water, and the names that they bear are recorded in instruments that the base maintains and that the agreements require and that the funding renews, and the water that they crossed, which recognizes no such names, receives the record as it receives all records, which is to say partially and temporarily and with the particular indifference that salt water maintains toward all inscription.

To swell and to subside, to widen and to narrow, these are the motions that the sea performs and that the prose performs, and the craft that cross the sea and the craft that record the crossing and the craft that wait to cross move in these motions, which the documents name migration and the fishermen name tide and the patrols name situation and which the prose, in its own motion, names undulation, prefiguring what will follow, what has always followed, the complex field of encounter and evasion and assistance and interception and the waiting that precedes and follows each, the night that empties and fills and empties again, the horizon that promises and withdraws its promise, the water that teaches and instructs and guides and receives and keeps and returns, and returns, and returns.

The waters that the European border agency monitors and the currents that its algorithms predict and the thermal signatures that its aircraft register and the distress frequencies that its operators scan and the vessel positions that its satellites triangulate and the drift patterns that its models extrapolate—all these converge upon a limestone island that fishermen once called the gateway and cartographers now designate the frontier, where the African littoral dilates toward Sicilian headlands across a sea that swells and subsides according to seasons no treaty can amend, and where, to teach migrants safe embarkation and to instruct captains in humanitarian protocols and to demonstrate rescue techniques to coastal militias, the agency deploys exercises whose participants, assembled in bays and inlets, rehearse scenarios of drowning that no benevolent curriculum can prevent from becoming coercive spectacle, since the pedagogical gesture itself requires the production of bodies in water, bodies upon which the lesson depends, bodies that must be there to be saved in order that saving might be demonstrated, and that must be countable in order that counting might be verified, and that must be photographed in order that photography might circulate through the institutional archives where the benevolence is stored and retrieved and stored again, until the image and the act become indistinguishable from the system that produces them, and the system produces them because the image requires them, and the image requires them because the system has learned that images of bodies in water generate the funding that produces more images of bodies in water, in a recursion that no narratorial intervention interrupts, since the narrator too is positioned within the apparatus that sees and is seen, that monitors and is monitored, that records and is recorded, and that finds in this very positioning the material for its own continuation, its own expansion, its own justification as the only possible response to the sea that it has made visible and that visibility has made its own.

The island that rises from these waters, which the Phoenicians once traversed and the Romans fortified and the Arabs cultivated and the Normans consecrated and the Bourbons garrisoned and the Italians annexed and the Europeans now administer as an externalized border, bears in its harbors the vessels that perform this administration, and in its airstrips the aircraft that extend it, and in its detention facilities the bodies that confirm its necessity, and in its cemeteries the bodies that exceed its capacity, and in its museums the artifacts that commemorate what the administration has survived, and in its archives the documents that anticipate what it will become, all of which the present description records in the same continuous present that the sea maintains, the sea that knows no tense but its own, that swells and subsides without reference to human chronology, yet that the description must puncture with the acknowledgment that this present of writing is itself a particular present, located and datable, governed by verbs of ongoing change that the atemporal surround cannot accommodate without rupture.

The limestone absorbs the water and the water dissolves the limestone, and the dissolution produces the karst that channels the runoff, and the runoff erodes the channels deeper, and the deeper channels draw more water, and the more water accelerates the dissolution, in a binary coordination of element and element that repeats across the island's topography, in bays and inlets, in caves and sinkholes, in the swelling and subsiding of the water table that mirrors the swelling and subsiding of the sea itself, and that the island's inhabitants have learned to read as augury, as warning, as the body's own knowledge of what the administrative instruments will later confirm, the instruments that measure and record and transmit, that make the island visible to distant decision-makers who will never stand upon it, who will never feel its heat or smell its vegetation or hear its silences, yet who will determine what happens there, who will authorize the exercises and approve the budgets and review the statistics and extend the mandates, in a remote presence that the island feels as pressure, as weight, as the atmospheric condition of its own existence.

The administrative presence concentrates at the port, where the vessels dock and the aircraft land and the buses arrive and the containers are stored and the personnel are housed, and where the documentation is produced that transforms the island from one thing to another, from fishing community to border infrastructure, from tourist destination to humanitarian emergency, from national territory to European periphery, and back again, according to the instrument that governs the transformation, the instrument that is itself invisible, that marks no boundary in the physical world, yet that divides the world absolutely, so that the same body in the same water at the same moment is one thing before the instrument registers it and another thing after, and this transformation, which the instrument accomplishes without moving, without touching, without any intervention in the physical world, is the central mystery that the island daily enacts, the mystery that its inhabitants have learned not to question, since the questioning produces no answer that the instrument cannot absorb, cannot reclassify, cannot file according to its own protocols.

The sea that surrounds this port, that the port faces and fences and frames, alternates in the description between expansion and constriction, between the vocabulary of dilation and the vocabulary of compression, between the open horizon that the vessels seek and the narrow strait that they must negotiate, between the broad basin that the wind crosses and the tight channel that the current accelerates, between the wide water that the eye measures and the close wave that the hull receives, and this alternation runs the full arc of the description, beginning with expansion, moving to constriction, returning to expansion, as the sea itself teaches, as the sea itself performs in its own pedagogy of movement, its own curriculum of force and resistance, of surface and depth, of the visible and the invisible that the instruments attempt to render visible, that the thermal cameras detect and the radar registers and the sonar maps, yet that remains, beneath these registrations, something other than what they record, something that exceeds the record, that the record cannot capture without transforming, without reducing to the scale of its own resolution, its own bandwidth, its own capacity for storage and retrieval.

The thermal camera that detects the body in water and the photograph that preserves the detection and the archive that stores the photograph and the report that cites the archive and the policy that references the report and the budget that implements the policy and the exercise that spends the budget and the image that documents the exercise and the circulation that distributes the image and the public that receives the circulation and the opinion that the public forms and the election that the opinion influences and the government that the election produces and the appointment that the government makes and the directive that the appointment issues and the operation that the directive authorizes and the vessel that the operation deploys and the camera that the vessel carries and the body that the camera detects: this chain of specular doublings, each link reflecting and transforming what precedes it, each medium named in the text that describes it, each inversion marked by the technical specification of the medium itself, constitutes the optical system that the island has become, the system of seeing and being seen that determines what can happen there, what can be said about what happens there, what can be done in response to what is said.

The periodic syntax of this description, which now contracts and now expands, now nests deeply and now runs flat, now accumulates clauses in waves of subordination and now releases them into simple statement, now burrows inward toward depth eleven and now rests at depth one, this syntax that undulates across the passage in crest and trough, in swell and subside, in the very rhythm that the sea itself maintains, that the sea itself teaches as its own proper movement, this syntax prefigures what the narrative will unfold: the crossing that awaits, the vessel that will depart, the water that will be entered, the horizon that will be sought, the rescue that will be performed or failed, the arrival that will be documented or undocumented, the status that will be granted or refused, the return that will be enforced or evaded, the death that will be recorded or unrecorded, in a sequence that the syntax has already announced, that the syntax has already performed in its own formal procedure, its own curriculum of expansion and constriction, of the long period and the short, of the deeply embedded and the simply stated.
